lastText: The Night EndsThe Long SleepNew Ending Discovered · 1 / 15A SOLICITOR REMEMBERS A HOSTYou go home by the oldest road, and nobody follows. In the crypt the ten boxes are waiting. You lie down in the nearest and draw the lid over you, and the key stays in the lock on the inside. In the dark you think, as you have thought many times, of a young man at a window in the third week of May, with a bead of blood on his chin, and of the staircase. It is little to remember, and it is more than you thought you had kept. The tellings differ, but they agree on one thing: that whatever he did, he did it in a great hurry, as if he were afraid there would not be enough time. People remember that he wept. A girl from the village says that she saw him, on the night of the storm, standing on the cliff with his hands over his face.
